extraction_warnings: PDF uses concatenated code formats (e.g., '94011000', '940131', '94013100') without dots. These have been re-formatted to NNNN.NN.NN per the schema. 6-digit codes (e.g., '940210', '940290') interpreted as subheading-only group rows.

Note 1 contains exclusions labelled (a) through (m), with (ij) used in place of (i)+(j) per ITC-HS convention — preserved verbatim. Single-letter (i) is absent (skipped) and (j) is fused with (i) as 'ij'.

Note 1(g) reference structure is ambiguous in source: 'furniture specially designed as parts of apparatus of heading 8518 (heading 8518), of headings 8519 or 8521 (heading 8522) or of headings 8525 to 8528 (heading 8529)' — the parenthetical heading refers to where the excluded furniture is classified instead. Captured all three sub-redirects (8518, 8522, 8529).
Note 1(l) source text contains a likely typo: 'luminaries' (should likely read 'luminaires') — preserved verbatim from PDF.
Heading 9405 description in source PDF is in ALL CAPS while other heading descriptions are in Title Case. Preserved verbatim.

Subheading 9404.40 description in source PDF ends with a colon ('Quilts, bedspreads, eiderdowns and duvets (comforters):') — preserved verbatim; tariff lines 9404.40.10 through 9404.40.40 sit under it.

Tariff code 9403.91.00 carries policy condition column value 'Subject to Policy Condition 1 of this Chapter' (Red Sanders wood restriction). Only this code is explicitly flagged in the source PDF's policy condition column.
Policy Condition 1 (Red Sanders) does not have notification date or notification number columns populated in source PDF — null retained.

Note 1(d) bundles three exclusions in one clause: parts of general use (Section XV) of base metal, similar goods of plastics (Chapter 39), and safes (8303). Split into three exclusion entries for downstream routing.

Note 3 splits into two sub-clauses (A) and (B). Both retained verbatim under a single note_number='3' entry. Three derived exclusion entries created from Note 3 to capture Chapters 68, 69 and Heading 9404 cross-references.

Source PDF uses '- -' and '----' to indicate subheading hierarchy levels (e.g., '- - Of wood', '---- Of Rubber'). These dashes are preserved verbatim in tariff line descriptions; subheading descriptions normalised slightly for readability while keeping the discriminating tail (e.g., '-- Of wood').

Section title 'MISCELLANEOUS MANUFACTURED ARTICLES' inferred — the PDF header reads 'Section XX, MISCELLANEOUS MANUFACTURED ARTICLES'. No separate section_notes table appears in this single-chapter PDF, so section_notes is left empty.

chapter_notes.text: This Chapter does not cover : (a) pneumatic or water mattresses, pillows or cushions, of Chapter 39, 40 or 63; (b) mirrors designed for placing on the floor or ground [for example, cheval-glasses (swingmirrors)] of heading 7009; (c) articles of Chapter 71; (d) parts of general use as defined in Note 2 to Section XV, of base metal (Section XV), or similar goods of plastics (Chapter 39), or safes of heading 8303; (e) furniture specially designed as parts of refrigerating or freezing equipment of heading 8418; furniture specially designed for sewing machines (heading 8452); (f) lamps or light sources and parts thereof of Chapter 85; (g) furniture specially designed as parts of apparatus of heading 8518 (heading 8518), of headings 8519 or 8521 (heading 8522) or of headings 8525 to 8528 (heading 8529); (h) articles of heading 8714; (ij) dentists chairs incorporating dental appliances of heading 9018 or dentists spittoons (heading 9018); (k) articles of Chapter 91 (for example, clocks and clock cases); (l) toy furniture or toy, luminaries and lighting fittings (heading 9503), billiard tables or other furniture specially constructed for games (heading 9504), furniture for conjuring tricks or decorations (other than lightings strings) such as Chinese lanterns (heading 9505); or (m) monopods, bipods, tripods and similar articles (heading 9620).

The articles (other than parts) referred to in headings 9401 to 9403 are to be classified in those headings only if they are designed for placing on the floor or ground. The following are, however, to be classified in the above-mentioned headings even if they are designed to be hung, to be fixed to the wall or to stand one on the other: (a) Cupboards, bookcases, other shelved furniture (including single shelves presented with supports for fixing them to the wall) and unit furniture; (b) seats and beds.

(A) In headings 9401 to 9403 references to parts of goods do not include references to sheets or slabs (whether or not cut to shape but not combined with other parts) of glass (including mirrors), marble or other stone or of any other material referred to in Chapter 68 or 69. (B) Goods described in heading 9404, presented separately, are not to be classified in heading 9401, 9402 or 9403 as parts of goods.

For the purposes of heading 9406, the expression "prefabricated buildings" means buildings which are finished in the factory or put up as elements, presented together, to be assembled on site, such as housing or worksite accommodation, offices, schools, shops, sheds, garages or similar buildings. Prefabricated buildings include "modular building units" of steel, normally presented in the size and shape of a standard shipping container, but substantially or completely pre-fitted internally. Such modular building units are normally designed to be assembled together to form permanent buildings.
